subject.title: fix: discord exec approvals fails against local self-signed TLS gateway

question: Should maintainers repair/review https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/80204 as the shared bootstrap TLS fingerprint fix, or replace it with a clean equivalent?
rationale: The remaining work changes certificate fingerprint trust routing for Gateway clients, and the active PR is conflicting with a known stale import blocker, so a maintainer should own the security-boundary review path.

options.title: Repair and review active PR
options.body: Resolve conflicts and the stale import blocker in the open shared-bootstrap PR, then validate local, remote, env, CLI, and non-WSS TLS fingerprint semantics before merge.

options.title: Replace with a clean successor
options.body: Open a narrow replacement that preserves the same shared-bootstrap fix intent if the active branch remains hard to reconcile.

options.title: Hold for TLS policy redesign
options.body: Keep the issue open without landing until maintainers revisit local, remote, CLI, and env TLS pin precedence as a broader policy decision.

recommendation.title: Repair and review active PR
recommendation.body: Resolve conflicts and the stale import blocker in the open shared-bootstrap PR, then validate local, remote, env, CLI, and non-WSS TLS fingerprint semantics before merge.

likelyOwner.reason: Prior Gateway TLS fingerprint and shared approval helper history make this the strongest available routing owner for the trust-boundary decision.
